description: Historical patterns remain broadly useful but complacency may hide structural change.
Rapid AI cyber automation platform and biotechnology change outpace governance and accountability.
Climate nonstationarity creates compound hazards and infrastructure planning uncertainty.
Conflict sanctions trade disruption cyber risk and bloc formation intensify strategic uncertainty.
Debt liquidity asset repricing climate exposure and confidence dynamics spread through financial systems.
Institutional capacity legitimacy finance workforce and coordination deteriorate under stress.
Cross-domain failure links climate finance infrastructure health technology and political instability.
Monitoring learning accountability and adaptive pathways reduce preparedness gaps under uncertainty.
